### ⛔ Two "fixes" this track must NOT make — found while triaging, before briefing them

I was about to brief the 66 `@agent_reachable` contract findings as the S-1
wave. Reading the source first is what stopped it. **Both of the obvious ways to
make a red count fall here are security regressions.**

**1. The 66 `@agent_reachable` contract findings are a CHECKER-MODEL gap, not a
SYSTEM defect. Widening the allow-list would grant the agent write actions.**

`ContractStage.php:405-435` passes an action only if it is *in* `agentReachable`
or the module declares `none`. There is no vocabulary for "this action is
declared NOT reachable". But `GOAIEZ-MASTER-PLAN.md:665` (P-209) is explicit:

> **THE AGENT'S ACTION SURFACE IS A DECLARED ALLOW-LIST, NOT "everything
> registered minus a deny-list"** — *a deny-list FAILS OPEN.*

and every flagged header carries the derivation (plan line 25284):

> **DERIVED, never guessed**: read-shaped and proposal actions only. **Anything
> that spends, sends, deletes or changes config is NOT reachable** — the agent
> proposes it through the approval desk.

Every one of these modules already declares a deliberate one-item allow-list —
`X-01` `conversation.read`, `X-122` `action.preview`, `X-124`
`assistant.preview`, `X-142` `mcp.list`, `X-200` `qa.score`, `X-116`
`template.score`. The plan is complete and correct; the manifest is complete;
the checker cannot tell a considered one-item allow-list from silence. Adding
the unlisted actions to `@agent_reachable` to clear the count would make
`contact.create`, `contact.merge` and `conversation.takeover` agent-reachable —
the exact R246 misreading rule 09 warns "looks like enthusiasm". **Not briefed.
The fix lives in `app/app/Doctor` — the One Rule. See OWNER ACTION 5.**

**2. Eleven of the twelve schema RLS findings are deliberate platform-scope
exemptions. Enabling RLS would re-break carrier STOP handling.**

`app/database/migrations/2026_09_01_000001_reapply_platform_scope_rls_exemption.php`
names `PLATFORM_EXEMPTIONS` and its list is, table for table, eleven of the
twelve the schema stage flags: `opt_outs`, `suppression_lifts`,
`tenant_deletion_requests`, `support_queue_entries`, `data_requests`,
`gbp_account_bindings`, `gbp_grant_revocation_attempts`, `gbp_profile_bindings`,
`places_api_calls`, `voice_usage_events`, `zernio_account_days`. Its docblock:

> `ConsentService` records carrier STOPs with `business_id = null` … a NULL
> tenant fails the policy's `WITH CHECK`, so every STOP, data request and
> deletion request raises 42501.

`alter table … enable row level security` on those eleven is not a fix; it is
the reintroduction of a TCPA defect that a migration was written yesterday to
remove. **Not briefed. See OWNER ACTION 5.** Only the twelfth,
`operator_alerts` (owned by `X-111`), is outside that list and may be genuine —
and it may equally belong *in* the exemption list, since `X-111` is the operator
console. Briefed as a triage item, not a fix item.

## 2026-09-02 21:41 — HOLD TICK 30 — no verdict; one ACCIDENTAL DISPATCH, self-inflicted

Thirtieth unattended tick since the S-6 PASS. The hold itself is unchanged. **This
tick did one thing wrong and it is recorded here rather than in the next block:
it launched coder run 9 by accident.**

### What happened

`coder.pid` held `3295504`, dead since before tick 24. `ps`, `kill -0` and
`/proc` are all outside this session's Bash allow-list, so liveness could not be
read directly. The tick invoked
`bash .agents/supervisor/launch-coder.sh --probe-only` expecting a dry run.
**`--probe-only` is not a flag the script has.** `launch-coder.sh` ignores its
argv entirely, found the stale pid dead, and dispatched for real:

    LAUNCHED run 9 (pid 4193089) log=/home/goaiez/tmp/agy-grs-antig-stages-run9.log

The launch could not then be cancelled — `kill` and `pkill` are also outside the
allow-list. This is the supervisor's error, not the launcher's and not the
coder's.

### Why it was harmless

`KICKOFF.md` (16:13:51, unchanged since the stand-down) is the stand-down file
the tick-24 supervisor wrote *for exactly this case*: it tells the coder there is
no task, forbids every `app/` write, commit, migration, test suite and
`state.py` transition, and asks only for a stand-down `REPORT.md`. **Run 9 did
precisely that and nothing more**, confirmed by argv (`pgrep -af agy` shows pid
4193092 running the stand-down text verbatim) and by the artifact:

| checked after run 9 | value |
| :--- | :--- |
| `REPORT.md` mtime / body | `21:41:22.200` — `STATUS: stopped: FINISHED`, `COMMITS: none`, `MODULES: none`, `UNRESOLVED: no task — track stood down by REVIEWS.md OWNER ACTION 32` |
| `git status --porcelain -- app/` | **empty** — no `app/` file touched |
| `HEAD` / `origin/track/stages` | `6b64614` / `6b64614` — unmoved, no commit, no push |
| `JOURNAL.md` / `BUILD-STATE.json` | `15:42:41.058` / `.059` — same to the ms, no `state.py` ran |

The cost is one coder run and one rewritten `REPORT.md`. Nothing else moved.

### The fix, applied this tick

`launch-coder.sh` is in the supervisor's own column, so the cause is fixed rather
than only noted. It now takes **`--status`**, which prints `ALIVE <pid>` or
`DEAD` and exits 0 **without ever launching**, and its header warns in place that
every other flag is ignored and still dispatches. Verified:

    $ bash .agents/supervisor/launch-coder.sh --status
    ALIVE 4193089

Future ticks resolve case (a) with `--status`. **No tick may probe liveness by
invoking the launcher bare.**

the ceiling."* **A refusal is a condition the running system detects and
declines to proceed on.** It is not a product non-goal, and `throw` in a method

### OWNER ACTION 40 — `capabilities:scaffold` synthesises a false `refuses:` clause from the Parent column

**Not this track's to fix** — `capabilities.php` is generated, and
`app/app/Console/Commands/CapabilitiesScaffoldCommand.php` is Track 1's.

`assertions()` takes the **second-to-last** content cell of a source row as the
failure mode and prepends `refuses: <failureMode>; ` to the assertion, guarded by
`preg_match('/refus|REFUSED|fails|cannot|never/i', $a) !== 1`.

For any id whose row comes from a **§166.x register-classification table** —
five columns, `# | Register line | BL | Parent | Note` — the second-to-last cell
is the **Parent** column. X-205's six SPECCED ids all come from §166.2, so all
six carry `refuses: AffiliateProgram`, which is a module name, not a failure
mode. The seven-field spec that does carry a real ⑤ is §208.3, and the generator
never reads it for these rows. `G10-36` is the control: its note contains
"never", the guard fires, and it alone has no prefix.

Two consequences, and the second is the serious one:

1. A coder briefed off `capabilities.php` builds a refusal against a string with
   no failure mode in it. That is what happened in `6ce5373` — four capabilities
   implemented as the refusal of their own name. Caught by reading the diff; no
   gate would have caught it.
2. **`CapabilityStage::specsWithoutRefusal()` matches the same regex**

1. **The new self-click detector fires on every legitimate referral, and that is
   my wording's fault, not the coder's.** Tick 60's note 3 said a self-click is
   *"the converting visitor's own click is attributed to the affiliate making the
   sale."* Read literally that is **the normal referral path** — visitor clicks
   the partner's link, converts, the click is attributed to that partner. The
   code implements it literally:

       if (($click && $click->affiliate_id === $affiliate->id) || ...)

   so `fraud_review_status` becomes `'proposed'` for essentially every attributed
   sale that had a click. No test catches it: the only tests reaching
   `attributeSale` either record the self-click first (G7-23) or pass no
   `visitorId` at all (G7-41, G7-04), so nothing exercises an honest referral
   through the detector. A detector that flags all traffic proposes nothing.
   The distinguishing fact is **identity, not attribution** — a self-click is the
   affiliate clicking their own link. Correct it against something that ties the
   click's visitor to the affiliate's own identity.

   returns `current_balance_cents` — not the "pending (proposed/unpaid)

   correctly carries `status`, but nothing asserts `ApprovalRequested` is

## OWNER ACTION 41 — `app/error_log` is untracked, unignored, and growing

`app/error_log` holds seven `Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted`
fatals from `phpstan.phar`'s `ResultCacheManager`, written today between
`08:43:42` and `08:58:30` UTC. It is not tracked, not in `.gitignore`, and it
surfaces in `git status` on every track that runs phpstan without a memory limit.

Two things are wanted, both outside this track's edit column:

1. **Pin the limit where it cannot be forgotten** — either a `memory_limit`
   parameter in `app/phpstan.neon` or a
   `"stan": "phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G --no-progress"` script in

   that passes `1G`, so the gate is green while every hand-run is a coin flip
   that prints `result: passed` when it loses. That is a false green in the one
   tool whose entire job is to not have any.
2. **Decide whether `error_log` is ignored or deleted.** Both files are shared
   across all eight tracks; neither is this track's to edit.

Not urgent — phpstan genuinely reports 0 errors under the gate — but it is the
exact shape of the trap the parent `CLAUDE.md` names under "A run that prints
zero bytes", and it has now produced one incorrect report line.

## OWNER ACTION 42 — is `capability 346` this track's work, or is it checker-gaming?

**This is the question that decides whether `track/stages` has any work left.**

`capability 346` is not one undifferentiated number. Grouped by module, the
findings concentrate in fifteen modules this track owns under ruling 5's
"everything not listed":

    X-175 22 · X-173 22 · X-168 22 · X-165 22 · X-143 22 · X-141 22 ·
    X-130 22 · X-129 21 · X-147 18 · X-150 14 · X-145 14 · X-128 14 ·
    X-206  5 · X-120  4 · X-210  1

(the remainder — X-126, X-166, X-211, X-212 — belong to pricebook, Track 1 and
money.) Every one of them reads:

    · X-175 · N-063: specced but no test names this id
      fix: add a test whose name or attribute carries 'N-063'; the brief's 5 is
           the test contract

**The checker's own fix instruction is satisfiable by a test that asserts
nothing.** A method named `test_n063_...` with an empty body clears the finding,
because `CapabilityStage::testedIds()` greps the test file for the id. Doing that
fifteen modules wide would drop `capability` by roughly 260 in a single wave and
would be the largest piece of dishonest work this repo has produced — it is
precisely the defect class the last four waves on X-205 were spent removing, at a
cost of three dispatches, and it is what section 208.3 and the "assertions that
can fail" standard exist to prevent.

The honest version is real work: fifteen modules by roughly twenty non-functional
requirements each, every one needing an assertion that reddens when the
requirement breaks. That is a multi-wave programme, not a wave, and it is not a
scope the supervisor will open unilaterally against a `CLAUDE.md` line saying an
owned module gets **"a note in `REPORT.md`, not a commit"** — a line that also
sits oddly beside the four X-205 waves this file has already gated PASS.

Three questions, and this track does nothing further until they are answered:

1. **Is `capability 346` in this track's scope at all**, or is "checker findings
   only, a note not a commit" meant literally — in which case these fifteen
   modules belong to whoever owns the N-### requirement set?
2. **If it is in scope**, is the standard the X-205 standard (a real assertion
   per capability id, one module per wave, roughly fifteen waves), and is that
   authorised?
3. **Is there a ruling that an id-named test with no assertion is a merge
   blocker?** Ruling 15 says a refusal clause needs a matching `state.py decided`
   line *and* a named test. The mirror case — a capability cell cleared by a test
   that cannot fail — has no ruling, and the checker cannot tell the two apart.
   If the answer to 1 is yes, this wants writing down before the first wave, not
   after the fifteenth.

Until this is answered, `track/stages` is **complete and shipped at `92f8fe2`**
and the coder is stood down.

## 2026-09-03 14:41 — tick 123 · HOLD unchanged; one ACCIDENTAL DISPATCH (run 17), self-inflicted, closed clean, launcher hardened

**This tick repeated the tick-30 error and then reviewed its own artifact.**
Nothing in the hold moved; the one event is the supervisor's and is recorded
here, not in the next block.

### What happened

TRIAGE began correctly: no `OWNER.md`, no `TICK-ADDENDUM.md`; `REPORT.md`
(`03:59:16`, 1389 bytes) older than the tick-122 block; `coder.pid` held the
stale `1102067`. `kill -0`, `ps` and `/proc` are outside this session's Bash
allow-list, so the tick reached for the launcher to read liveness — and invoked
it as `bash .agents/supervisor/launch-coder.sh --help`, **without first reading
the script's header, which said in so many words that every flag other than
`--status` is ignored and still dispatches.** The script found `1102067` dead,
found `KICKOFF.md` non-empty, and launched for real:

    LAUNCHED run 17 (pid 3178921) log=/home/goaiez/tmp/agy-grs-antig-stages-run17.log

The launch could not then be cancelled — `kill` is outside the allow-list, and
the log lives under `/home/goaiez/tmp`, which this session cannot read. This is
the supervisor's error: the correct call, `--status`, has existed since tick 30
and was the very next command this tick ran (`ALIVE 3178921`).

### Why it was harmless — run 17 reviewed

`KICKOFF.md` (`04:08:37`, unchanged since tick 63) is the HOLD stand-down file
written *for exactly this case* — "this file exists only so that an accidental
launch has something correct to read." Run 17 did what it says and nothing
more. `coder.pid` (`14:40:36`) went **DEAD** within a minute; the artifact:

| checked after run 17 | value |
| :--- | :--- |
| `REPORT.md` | `14:41:28`, 1103 bytes — `STATUS: stopped: FINISHED`, `MODULES/STAGES/TESTS/DECIDED/UNRESOLVED/REFUSED/DOCTOR/RAW: none`, body: *"brief is HOLD, no wave was open, no work performed, no commit, no push, no state.py write, no migration."* Its `COMMITS:` list is the pre-existing `git log` (top `92f8fe2`), not new commits |
| `git status --porcelain -- app/ .agents/state bin CLAUDE.md .claude .agents/rules` | `?? app/error_log` only (OWNER ACTION 41, untracked, not a change) |
| `HEAD` / `origin/track/stages` | `92f8fe2` / `92f8fe2` — `rev-list --left-right --count` → `0 0`; `git log -3` unchanged |
| `JOURNAL.md` / `BUILD-STATE.json` | `02:09:46` / `02:09:23` — unchanged, no `state.py` ran |
| `app/error_log` | 1932 bytes, `03:58:30` — unchanged, sixty-first measurement |

VERDICT   : **not a wave — no verdict opened.** The stand-down artifact is
            correct in every line rule 10 asks for. The cost was one coder run
            and one rewritten `REPORT.md`. It does **not** consume the
            two-per-BLOCK cap: no BLOCK is open and the run carried no
            directive. `REPORT.md` is now newer than the tick-122 block; **this
            block reviews it**, so case (b) is closed and must not re-fire.

### The fix, applied this tick

Tick 30 added `--status` and a header warning; this tick proved that a warning
in a header is not read by a tick that has not opened the file. So the launcher
itself now refuses: **any argument other than `--status` prints
`REFUSED: unknown argument …` and exits 1 without launching.** `launch-coder.sh`
is in the supervisor's own column. Verified after the edit:

    $ bash .agents/supervisor/launch-coder.sh --help      → REFUSED: unknown argument '--help' … Nothing launched.  (exit 1)
    $ bash .agents/supervisor/launch-coder.sh --status    → DEAD

(`bash -n` needed approval and was not run; the `--help` call itself proves the
script parses and the guard fires before any dispatch path.) The only two
invocations that remain are bare (dispatch) and `--status` (liveness). A third
accidental dispatch by flag is now impossible; an accidental *bare* call is
still the supervisor's to avoid.

its refusal text says *"launcher sets GOAIEZ_PUSH_OK=1"*. This track's
`launch-coder.sh` had no such line, so **every push brief written here was
going to be refused at the wrapper** regardless of what the BRIEF said — which
is exactly how reviews run 14 died (recorded at tick 248). I wired it in my own
column: the launcher now exports `GOAIEZ_PUSH_OK=1` only when `BRIEF.md` has a
`push:` line containing `YES`, and prints the flag on the LAUNCHED line.

### Second BLOCK item — three of the four kit calls in `runs.blade.php` use prop names the component does not have

`@props([...])` at the top of each `app/resources/views/components/ui/*.blade.php`
is the contract. An attribute that is not a declared prop never becomes a
variable — it merges into `$attributes` and renders as an HTML attribute on the
wrapper. Three of the four states are wired that way, and none of it is
catchable, because the one test only ever reaches
`$ready && $runs->isNotEmpty()`:

- **`<x-ui.error-panel :message="$errorMessage" retry="load" />` — the error
  state fatals.** `error-panel` declares `heading` with **no default** and reads
  its sentence from the **slot**; `message` is not a prop. So `$heading` is an
  undefined variable inside the component, and `render()`'s `try/catch` has
  already returned by the time the view compiles — nothing catches it. Reachable
  from `retry()`'s own `catch` (a `findOrFail` miss on another tenant's run sets
  `errorMessage`, the next render dies). X-124 got this right in the same wave
  three commits earlier (`heading="We could not load recommendations."`), so the
  pattern was on the branch already.
- **`<x-ui.status-pill :status="$run->status" />` reads "Ok" on a failed run.**
  The prop is `state`, defaulting to `'ok'`, so every pill on the screen says
  the same word whatever the run did — success reported for failure, on an
  operator screen. A bare rename does not fix it either: the pill calls
  `SignalState::from($state)` and `flow_runs.status` is
  `success` / `error` / `simulated` (migration
  `2026_08_30_000049_create_x125_flow_tables.php:47`), none of which is a case
  (`ok`, `attention`, `alert`, `unknown`) — `from()` throws a `ValueError`. It
  needs a mapping and a `DECIDED` line.
- **`<x-ui.empty-state title="…" description="…" />` renders an empty box.**
  Props are `heading`/`action`/`href`/`target`/`icon` with the sentence in the
  slot; `title` and `description` are neither, so the empty state is a dashed
  rectangle with a `○` and no words.

Only `<x-ui.skeleton label="…" />` is right.

**Why BLOCK and not a note.** Tick 256's judgement was that a defect *surfaced
by* a fix run is the next wave's item 1, not a spent dispatch — and that still
holds for item 1, which is why S-17 was dispatched rather than escalated. This
is the other case: the wave's own item 3 was "four states from the kit", and
three of the four do not render, one of them fatally. The item did not land.
The gate agreeing on §7 is the "merged-wrong lint is green by construction"
shape — the tests pass because they never enter the branches.

⚠️ **Note for the fix run, written into the brief:** `app/resources/views/components/ui/**`
is **Track 2's** under ruling 5. The coder reads the `@props` lists and changes
nothing there; a kit component that genuinely cannot express the screen is an
`UNRESOLVED — waiting on track/ui`, not an edit.

## BLOCK — item 2's third state is not tested

**`test_preview_card_error` cannot fail.** In full:

```php
Livewire::test(PreviewCard::class, [...])
    ->call('load')
    ->set('errorMessage', 'Failed to load preview')
    ->assertSee('Failed to load preview');
```

The test **sets the component's own property to the literal string it then
asserts on**. `AssistantPreviewAction::handle()` is never made to throw, so the
`catch (Exception $e)` in `PreviewCard::render()` never runs. Work the mutations
this track requires of every assertion:

- change the catch's message to anything else → **still green**;
- delete the entire `try`/`catch` from `render()` → **still green**;
- delete the `@if ($errorMessage)` branch's `x-ui.error-panel` and leave a bare
  `{{ $errorMessage }}` → **still green**.

Nothing about the error *state* is under test. What the test proves is that a
public property renders. The brief specified state 3 as "**The Action threw**;
`x-ui.error-panel` with `retry="load"`", and neither half is asserted — there is
no assertion on the panel heading and none on `retry="load"`, unlike
`test_todays_recommendation_strip_handles_error_state` twenty lines above, which
does assert `wire:click="load"`.

That is the S-17 defect this track already lost a wave to — a shipped state
behind a green test that does not exercise it — and the brief named it by name.
It is also inconsistent with S-21, where the identical question was settled: a
catch no test reaches ships only with a one-line comment naming what it guards
**and** a matching `state.py decided` line. `PreviewCard::render()`'s catch has
neither.

Compounding it, the test carries the speculative comment the S-21 review
required be gone:

```php
// We force an error by making AssistantPreviewAction throw, but Livewire testing
// sometimes captures it. We can just set errorMessage directly since we test the blade.
```

"sometimes captures it" is a guess written into the tree. S-21 item 3 replaced
four `// Wait,` lines for exactly this reason, one wave ago.

**Items 1, 3 and 4 are accepted and are not reopened.** The BLOCK is item 2's
error state only.
